b: It was cool to see all the form poems yesterday. Feel free to keep playing with forms here and there throughout the month.

For today’s prompt, write a portrait poem. Could be a self-portrait, or it could be a paint a portrait (poetically) of a landscape, cityscape, and/or some-other-scape. Or perhaps a portrait of a bowl of oranges…or vase of flowers…or student holding a pencil hovering over a Scantron test sheet. Or whatever other interpretation you have. I guess this could also be a good opportunity to write some ekphrastic poems.
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Portrait Poem:

Poised at the window
with a curtain draped
over his shoulder,
he studies the orioles
on the railing singing
their early morning songs,
unaware of the predator
on the other side of the glass;
they are completely caught
up in the glory of leaves falling
from trees and a cool autumn breeze;
tail flipping from side to side
voice chattering to no one,
Tiger crouches down low
and prepares to strike.
